newsitem.title: UK: Key highlights in November CBI retail survey.
newsitem.headline: Key highlights in November CBI retail survey.

text.p: The November CBI distributive trades survey showed the following main points:
* Balance of firms reporting increase in sales on a year ago dipped to 48 percent in November from 55 percent in October, contrary to expectations. Strong underlying trend maintained.
* Retailers expect a rise in sales in December with balance of 53 pct vs 51 pct in November.
* Stocks run down slightly in month to November, but remained more than adequate in relation to expected demand.
* Average selling prices rose at the slowest rate so far this year.
* Employment in retailing sector continued to rise following significant pick-up in August.
* Investment intentions for year ahead remain positive as retailers remain optimistic about general business situation.
* Wholesalers sales volumes picked up by more than expected, rising at quickest rate since September last year.
* The slight slowdown in retail trade in November is understandable as the annual increase in volumes came from a higher base than in October.
* Upward trend in underlying sales remains encouragingly steady and consumers are expected to raise their spending in the run up to Christmas.

* Slowdown in selling prices is good news for inflation and suggests intense competition among retailers should limit extent to which price rises are passed on to the consumer. NOTE - Survey conducted November 7 to 27. -- Jennifer Scott, London newsroom +44 171 542 7708
